Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden onset inability to move left arm upon waking (~1 hour prior to call), with no associated pain.
- Additional symptoms since onset: Tingling on left side of face; difficulty swallowing; speech slowing and increased effort.
- Denies facial asymmetry, hand discoloration, or abnormal temperature.
- No prior similar episodes.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented), Losartan (dose/route/frequency not documented), Amlodipine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Penicillin.
- Family history: Father with heart disease (further details unknown).
- Social history: Lives alone; former smoker; consumes beer (pints), “few drinks over the weekend” and occasionally during the week.

Objective:
- Unable to move left arm.
- No left arm pain reported.
- Sensory: Tingling on left side of face.
- Speech: Patient reports slowness and increased effort; was able to communicate on telephone.
- Swallowing: Patient reports difficulty.
- No observed or reported facial asymmetry.
- No reported discoloration or coldness in left hand.
- Mental state: Alert and oriented, able to answer questions.
- Vital signs, direct physical examination, and imaging not obtained (telephone consult).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Sudden-onset left-sided neurologic deficit:
   - Assessment: Suspected acute cerebrovascular accident (stroke).
   - Differential diagnosis: None documented.
   - Investigations planned: Emergency assessment at hospital (to include imaging and possible stroke work-up).
   - Treatment planned: Emergency ambulance arranged; hospital admission for further assessment and potential acute stroke management.
   - Relevant referrals: Emergency services (ambulance); likely neurology/stroke specialist at hospital.
